blindSummary:
This country presents extreme risk to trans visitors. A penal-code provision criminalises gender nonconformity directly, and sodomy carries life imprisonment (capital and corporal punishment removed in the 2020 reforms); a rights research publication documents state violence against LGBTQIA+ people, including extrajudicial killings. Since April 2023 the country has been in a catastrophic civil war between the national army and a large paramilitary force, with documented mass atrocities — the conflict intensifies every risk and eliminates any recourse. There is no legal gender recognition and no community infrastructure.

For a visitor: statutory criminalisation of gender nonconformity plus one of the world's worst active conflicts.
blindOutOfScope: War conditions affect all travellers; the gender-nonconformity law is trans-specific.
blindSourceSummaries: Rights research publication's country review: a penal-code provision criminalises gender nonconformity ('indecent' clothing - 40 lashes or a fine); documented state violence against LGBTQIA+ people including extrajudicial killings; gender-affirming healthcare constrained and no legal recognition; the ongoing conflict intensifies challenges; state reliance on official religious legal rulings obstructs transition.

International legal-aid trust country profile: this country criminalises same-sex sexual activity between men and between women, with sentences including a maximum of life imprisonment (and historically the death penalty for a third offence). (Only the opening was retrievable at fetch time.)

A foreign government's 2010 human-rights report on this country: documents the long-ruling former regime's abuses - extrajudicial killings, torture, an armed conflict in outlying regions, and the LGBT section noting criminalisation under the sodomy provision with flogging and death-penalty clauses.

Research study (2014) by a university research fellow with activists of a regional LGBTQI organisation serving two neighbouring countries of the same river basin - survival stories of gay men in this country and a neighbouring state: daily struggles, discrimination and violence rooted in societal gender and sexual norms, and whether post-2011 uprising change will transform circumstances.

Community magazine run by this country's LGBTI organisation: LGBTI rights here - history and analysis, organisation profile, and posts on regional LGBTI news and sexuality in the region's ancient civilizations - an LGBTI community resource.

Global de-criminalisation news site (July 2020): this country dropped the death penalty for homosexuality - the transitional ruling council also eliminated 100 lashes, leaving up to 5 years for a first offence, 7 for a second, life for a third; the regional LGBTQI organisation hailed the reforms as a major step toward judicial reform; the sodomy provision remains in force; only six nations then retained the death penalty for gay sex.
blindTangential: Sodomy carries life imprisonment — a direct risk for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
